Subject: Order Form + DPA: Annex questions & SCCs preference

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Our legal team is starting to work the redlines on the Order Form and DPA and we have a few open items before we can circulate to procurement: 

- SCCs: can Redwood confirm which version of the EU SCCs you plan to sign? Our preferred baseline is the 2021 SCCs but we need to know if Redwood will accept the controller-to-processor module (and the additional data transfer paragraph we typically add).
- Processor roles: we want a clear statement in the DPA that Redwood is a processor and that HealthNova remains controller. Also need a short list of subprocessor categories and any named subprocessors for EU-based processing.
- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): do you provide a separate TIA or an appendix to the DPA? We will need one alongside any SCCs.
- Data export and retention: we proposed a tighter export notification (48h notice for export requests) — is that acceptable?

We attached a tracked redline with our suggested changes. Could you loop in your legal contact and advise on timeline? Ideally we want to get to an executable Order Form + DPA within two weeks.

Subject: RE: Order Form + DPA: Annex questions & SCCs preference

Hi Emma — thanks for sending the redlines. I reviewed your tracked doc and propose the following approach to keep things moving: 

1) SCCs: Redwood will sign the 2021 EU SCCs (Controller -> Processor module) with the following clarifications included in the DPA Annex:
   - We accept a customer-provided transfer clause limited to the extent it mirrors the SCCs and does not create conflicting obligations on Redwood.
   - We will include a short supplementary clause describing technical measures (encryption in transit + at rest, key management summary).

2) Processor / Subprocessor mapping:
   - Statement: Redwood = Processor; HealthNova = Controller.
   - We will attach a categories-of-subprocessors exhibit listing: cloud infrastructure providers (IaaS), managed inference providers, logging/monitoring vendors, analytics providers.
   - Named EU subprocessors (current): GCP europe-west1 (via managed infra partner), S3-compatible backup provider (eu-central). We will provide the formal list as an exhibit.

3) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA):
   - We provide a TIA as an annex to the DPA. The annex will: summarize jurisdictions where transfers may occur, provide our legal risk assessment, and set out supplementary safeguards (e.g., encryption, contractually required vendor assessments).

4) Export notification / retention:
   - We cannot commit to 48h operational support for ad-hoc exports. Proposal: Redwood will provide a 5 business-day turnaround for export fulfillment for standard exports; for expedited exports (48h) we can offer an add-on support SKU or committed response for enterprise customers. We will add a short SLA table to the Order Form Appendix.

Next steps I propose: 
- Marissa: circulate a DPA + TIA markup (attached) with tracked changes (attached: dpa_annex_markups.docx).
- Emma / HealthNova: confirm whether you will accept the 5 business-day standard export window or require expedited support and whether you want named subprocessors added now or via exhibit post-signature.
- Logistics: if acceptable, Ben to propose final orderform execution window and we can send DocuSign.

Attachments: dpa_annex_markups.docx (docx); redwood_dpa_template.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if your team prefers to talk through the TIA details.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
